theorem.statement:
There exists one total Borel measurable radius \(R_\ell\), namely the pilot-split radius in \(\mathrm{def:pilot\mbox{-}split\mbox{-}certified\mbox{-}radius}\), using pilot sizes \(\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) and \(\lceil m_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\), main-sample centers, exclusion budget \(\beta_\ell=(n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)^{-2}\), deterministic ordering and tie-breaking, exhaustive compatible support-cluster, covariance-rank, and simplex-face enumeration, and certified rational interval arithmetic.  It satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{\ell\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}
 \Pr_P\{(\tau_{t,\ell})_{t>T_0}\in\mathcal C_\ell(R_\ell)\}
 \geq1-\alpha,
\]
and its confidence-set diameter is \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\).  On every supported fixed local stratum, the DKW branch has probability \(o(1)\), the pilot region converges in the quotient parameterization, every bounded within-cell root-\(m_\ell\) offset is learned, every cross-cell translation and finite simplex-face offset remains in \(\Gamma_\eta\), and
\[
 R_\ell^2/a_\ell\longrightarrow c^*(\eta,\alpha)
 \quad\text{in conditional probability given }\mathscr S_\eta.
\]
Only on a fixed stratum with unscaled knot separation, all weights bounded away from simplex faces, and a continuous nondegenerate critical law does the nuisance region collapse and the radius reduce to the corresponding separated oracle cutoff.  At collisions or faces the common nuisance supremum is retained; in particular, the Bernoulli collision honesty penalty cannot be removed by oracle adaptation.
theorem.proof_tex:
We first distinguish the causal target from the observed-law construction.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:stable\mbox{-}quantile\mbox{-}span}\) gives, for every post period,
\[
 \tau_{t,\ell}=Q^I_{0t,\ell}-Q^N_{0t,\ell}
 =Q^I_{0t,\ell}-\sum_{j=1}^Jw_{\ell j}Q_{jt,\ell}.
\tag{23}
\]
Thus the empirical DSC curve is an estimator of (23); it is not made causal by definition.  Positivity and rank enter through \(f\geq f_{\min}>0\) and \(H_\ell|_L\succeq\lambda I_L\), respectively, while finite post support and the common range bound enter through the endpoint representation.

Use the deterministic split and the radius defined in \(\mathrm{def:pilot\mbox{-}split\mbox{-}certified\mbox{-}radius}\).  Empirical order statistics are Borel functions.  The primitive intervals, finite label enumeration, rational grids, interval operations, first-success rule, and DKW fallback are Borel by \(\mathrm{lem:pilot\mbox{-}geometry\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}transfer}\).  Therefore \(R_\ell\) is a total Borel function taking values in \([0,2D]\).

Let \(\mathcal E^P_\ell\) be the pilot inclusion event in (18).  Conditional on the pilot and on \(\mathcal E^P_\ell\), the true finite-array quotient parameter belongs to \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\).  Let \(L^{M,\mathrm{raw}}_\ell\) denote the maximum, over post periods, of the squared main-center error divided by \(a^M_\ell\).  Apply the exact expansion \(\mathrm{thm:finite\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}source\mbox{-}expansion}\) to the main blocks.  Since \(N_{n,\ell}/n_\ell\to1\) and \(N_{m,\ell}/m_\ell\to1\), its remainder is still \(o_{\Pr}(1)\) after division by \(a^M_\ell\), uniformly over \(\mathcal M\).  The transfer inequality (21), the cushion (22), and the fact that \(\overline c_\ell\) is an upper certified common cutoff give
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}
 \Pr_P\{L^{M,\mathrm{raw}}_\ell
       \leq\overline c_\ell+\delta_\ell\mid\text{pilot}\}
 \geq1-\alpha-e_\ell
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E^P_\ell,
\tag{24}
\]
where
\[
 e_\ell=C\beta_\ell+C\zeta_\ell
       +C(L_{G,R}\gamma_\ell)^{1/2}longrightarrow0.
\tag{25}
\]
The coupling/transfer, linearization, nuisance-exclusion, Gaussian-tail, and interval errors appear separately in (19), (22), (18), the choice of \(G,R\), and the bracket width \(\zeta_\ell\); (25) is their union bound.  Notice that (24) uses the Gaussian probability at the exact level \(1-\alpha\) and a vanishing additive loss cushion.  Therefore it remains valid when the critical law has an atom; no continuity at its quantile is silently assumed.

By definition of \(T^\circ_\ell\),
\[
 \max_{t>T_0}\|\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}\|_2
 \leq T^\circ_\ell+
       \max_{t>T_0}\|\widetilde\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}\|_2.
\tag{26}
\]
Hence the successful branch radius covers whenever the event in (24) occurs.  On a failed branch, \(\mathrm{thm:honest\mbox{-}rate\mbox{-}ball}\) gives finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).  Taking expectations in (24), using \(\Pr((\mathcal E^P_\ell)^c)\leq C\beta_\ell\), and then applying the subsequence principle proves
\[
 \liminf_{\ell\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}
 \Pr_P\{(\tau_{t,\ell})_{t>T_0}\in\mathcal C_\ell(R_\ell)\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\tag{27}
\]
Indeed, if (27) failed, a violating sequence of laws would have a local subsubsequence supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:local\mbox{-}subsequence\mbox{-}extraction}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}linearization}\); equations (18)--(26) on that subsubsequence contradict the violation.

We next prove the diameter order.  On the Gaussian tail box, \(\|V_h\|\leq2G/\lambda\), endpoint coefficients are bounded by \(D\), and the number of endpoints is fixed.  Outside the box, Gaussian second moments and Markov's inequality give a uniform \(O_{\Pr}(1)\) bound for the common cutoff.  Thus \(\overline c_\ell=O_{\Pr}(1)\).  Leaving out a pilot fraction changes a pre empirical process by
\[
 O_{\Pr}(\sqrt{r_{n,\ell}}/n_\ell)=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-5/8})
\]
and changes a post empirical CDF by \(O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-5/8})\).  The smooth inverse bound and the transport inequality used in \(\mathrm{thm:honest\mbox{-}rate\mbox{-}ball}\) imply
\[
 T^\circ_\ell=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-5/8}+m_\ell^{-5/16})
 =o_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})
\tag{28}
\]
uniformly.  Since \(a^M_\ell/a_\ell\to1\), the successful radius has order
\(\sqrt{a_\ell}=O(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\).  The fallback has the same order by \(\mathrm{thm:honest\mbox{-}rate\mbox{-}ball}\).  The product-ball diameter is twice its radius, proving the assertion.

Fix now a supported local stratum.  Pilot DKW and binomial widths tend to zero in unscaled coordinates.  Equations (16)--(17) show Hausdorff convergence of every bounded within-cell offset interval to its true value.  Interior weights and fixed unscaled knot gaps are eventually separated; local face offsets and cross-cell root-scale translations are never estimated and converge instead to their full compatible coordinates in \(\Gamma_\eta\).  Equations (10)--(11) consistently recover \(H,w^0,\Omega\) and every covariance entry, with all compatible limiting ranks retained until their eigenvalue intervals separate.  Consequently
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell/\{\text{irrelevant translations}\}
 \longrightarrow \{\eta\}\times\Gamma_\eta
\tag{29}
\]
in the Painleve--Kuratowski, equivalently finite-dimensional local Hausdorff, sense on each certified tail box.  The deterministic complexity bound makes work-budget fallback impossible; (18) makes primitive-certification fallback probability \(o(1)\).

The loss is continuous on every enumerated compact cell, and the compactification in \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}common\mbox{-}cutoff}\) is exact on the tail box.  Therefore (29), tail enlargement, and interval width \(\zeta_\ell\to0\) give
\[
 \overline c_\ell\longrightarrow c^*(\eta,\alpha)
 \quad\text{conditionally on }\mathscr S_\eta.
\tag{30}
\]
At an atom of the critical law, the upper bracket and additive cushion approach the same left cutoff from above, so (30) does not require quantile continuity.  Combining (22), (28), (30), and \(a^M_\ell/a_\ell\to1\) yields
\[
 \frac{R_\ell^2}{a_\ell}
 =\frac{a^M_\ell}{a_\ell}(\overline c_\ell+\delta_\ell)+o_{\Pr}(1)
 \longrightarrow c^*(\eta,\alpha)
\tag{31}
\]
in conditional probability.  If knots have fixed unscaled separation, their root-\(m_\ell\) gaps dominate \(R=O(\sqrt{\log(1/\zeta_\ell)})\); if every weight is bounded away from zero, all face offsets diverge beyond \(2G/\lambda\).  Only then does the nuisance set collapse.  Continuity and nondegeneracy of the resulting critical law permit the usual plug-in oracle quantile.  At a collision or face, the corresponding nuisance coordinate remains in \(\Gamma_\eta\).  The strict Bernoulli inequality in \(\mathrm{thm:bernoulli\mbox{-}honesty\mbox{-}penalty}\) then proves that replacing the common cutoff by the collision oracle would destroy uniform coverage.  This completes the proof.
theorem.justification: This theorem supplies the load-bearing total measurable procedure: pilot-compatible quotient regions and certified common-cutoff computation retain the nonestimable local nuisance coordinates while attaining the uniformly honest rate and the conditional deterministic-cutoff frontier.
theorem.gap: The measurable pilot split, uniform raw-to-Gaussian transfer, support/rank/face enumeration, explicit error budgets, and vanishing-fallback proof are not supplied by the separate DSC, conditional-Gaussian, active-set, or honesty references.
theorem.consumer: The construction permits an unsmoothed simultaneous \(L^2\) reanalysis of the Zhai et al. mosquito-abundance QTE curves relative to the donor-identified post-treatment no-intervention law, excluding their distinct binary elimination estimand.

added_lemmas.statement: Let the observations in every pre-period cell be split deterministically into a pilot block of size \(r_{n,\ell}=\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) and a main block of size \(N_{n,\ell}=n_\ell-r_{n,\ell}\), using the fallback whenever \(N_{n,\ell}\leq0\).  Uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), the main-sample pooled score has an asymptotic linear representation on \(L\) as a fixed finite sum of bounded centered cell influence vectors, with an \(o_{\Pr}(1)\) remainder and finite-array covariance \(\Omega_\ell\).  Its bounded-Lipschitz distance from \(N(0,\Omega_\ell)\) is bounded by a computable deterministic modulus tending to zero.  The pilot consistently estimates \(w_\ell\), \(H_\ell\), and \(\Omega_\ell\) uniformly.  Every subsequence extracted by \(\mathrm{lem:local\mbox{-}subsequence\mbox{-}extraction}\) has a further subsequence on which \(w_\ell\to w^0\in\Delta_J\), \(\Omega_\ell\to\Omega\), and the main score converges to \(g\sim N_L(0,\Omega)\).  On that further subsequence the strongly convex moving-face criterion has the same limit \(V_h\) as in \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(P_L=I_J-J^{-1}\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^\top\).  Because every feasible weight difference belongs to \(L\), replacing a donor-quantile vector by \(P_Lq_{t,\ell}\) leaves every score and quadratic on \(L\) unchanged.  After translating the common outcome interval, the range condition gives
\[
 \sup_{t,\ell,u}\|P_Lq_{t,\ell}(u)\|_2\leq \sqrt J D.
\tag{1}
\]
For a pre cell with distribution function \(F\), quantile \(Q\), and density \(f\), define the quantile influence function
\[
 \phi_F(x;u)=-\frac{\mathbf 1\{x\leq Q(u)\}-u}{f(Q(u))}.
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:smooth\mbox{-}pre}\) implies \(|\phi_F(x;u)|\leq f_{\min}^{-1}\).  Taylor's formula, including its one-sided endpoint version, gives
\[
 |F(Q(u)+z)-u-f(Q(u))z|\leq \tfrac12L_fz^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Apply (3) on the DKW event and control the empirical-process oscillation over intervals of length proportional to the DKW width by a dyadic grid and the binomial Bernstein bound.  Monotonicity fills the gaps between grid points.  Uniformly over the density class this yields
\[
 \left\|\sqrt N(\widehat Q-Q)-N^{-1/2}\sum_{k=1}^N
       \phi_F(X_k;\cdot)\right\|_{L^2}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(N^{-1/4}\{\log(e+N)\}^{3/4}\right)=o_{\Pr}(1).
\tag{4}
\]
For completeness, the grid calculation uses cells of width
\(N^{-1/2}\{\log(e+N)\}^{1/2}\); Bernstein's exponent on one such cell is proportional to its expected count, and summing the resulting geometric bounds over the dyadic levels gives the factor in (4).  All constants depend only on \(f_{\min},f_{\max},L_f,D\), so (4) is uniform.  This is the inverse-map derivative in \(\mathrm{lem:quantile\mbox{-}functional\mbox{-}delta\mbox{-}method}\), now with the uniform remainder required here.

Let \(\widehat q^M_{t,\ell}\) and \(\widehat Q^{N,M}_{0t,\ell}\) be the main-sample empirical quantiles and define
\[
 \widehat g^M_\ell=
 \sum_{t\leq T_0}\pi_t\int_0^1
 P_L\widehat q^M_{t,\ell}(u)\sqrt{N_{n,\ell}}
 \{\widehat Q^{N,M}_{0t,\ell}(u)-widehat q^M_{t,\ell}(u)^\top w_\ell\}\,du.
\tag{5}
\]
The exact stable-span assumption cancels the population residual in (5).  Substitution of (4), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz and the uniform \(L^2\) rate \(O_{\Pr}(N_{n,\ell}^{-1/2})\), gives
\[
 \widehat g^M_\ell=N_{n,\ell}^{-1/2}
      \sum_{t\leq T_0}\sum_{c\in\{0,1,\ldots,J\}}
      \sum_{k=1}^{N_{n,\ell}}\xi_{ct,\ell}(X_{ctk})+o_{\Pr}(1),
\tag{6}
\]
where the vectors \(\xi_{ct,\ell}\in L\) are obtained by integrating (2) against \(\pi_tP_Lq_{t,\ell}\), with coefficient one for the treated cell and coefficient \(-w_{\ell c}\) for donor cell \(c\).  Equations (1)--(2), \(0\leq w_{\ell c}\leq1\), and fixed \(J,T_0\) give a deterministic bound
\[
 \max_{c,t,\ell,x}\|\xi_{ct,\ell}(x)\|_2
 \leq C_{mathrm{pre}}(J,T_0,D,f_{\min}).
\tag{7}
\]
Define \(\Omega_\ell\) as the covariance of the linear term in (6).  Independence across cells makes it the sum of the cell covariances and proves that it is positive semidefinite.

We record a quantitative triangular-array argument because covariance rank is not assumed fixed.  For fixed \(z\in L\), third-order Taylor expansion and (7) imply
\[
 \log \mathbb E\exp\{iz^\top N_{n,\ell}^{-1/2}\!\sum\xi\}
 =-\tfrac12z^\top\Omega_\ell z
   +O\!\left(\|z\|_2^3N_{n,\ell}^{-1/2}\right),
\tag{8}
\]
uniformly in the law, without dividing by an eigenvalue of \(\Omega_\ell\).  Convolution with a compactly supported smooth kernel, Fourier inversion on a ball, and (8) give, in the fixed dimension \(J-1\),
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L\!left(N_{n,\ell}^{-1/2}\sum\xi\right),
 N(0,\Omega_\ell)\right)
 \leq C_{mathrm{pre}}N_{n,\ell}^{-1/[4(J+3)]}.
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, the Fourier error on a ball of radius \(T\) is at most
\(C T^{J+2}N_{n,\ell}^{-1/2}\), the smoothing error is at most \(C/T\), and the nonoptimal choice \(T=N_{n,\ell}^{1/[4(J+3)]}\) proves (9).  Combining (4), (6), and the usual Lipschitz smoothing inequality proves the asserted computable bounded-Lipschitz modulus.  Since (8) remains valid for singular limits, this also proves the required uniform triangular central limit theorem.

It remains to show that the covariance entering the certification is estimable.  On the pilot block take the symmetric difference quotient of the empirical CDF with bandwidth equal to the square root of its simultaneous DKW width, use the one-sided difference at a boundary, and truncate the result to \([f_{\min},f_{\max}]\).  On the DKW event, (3) gives
\[
 \sup_x|\widehat f(x)-f(x)|
 \leq 2\|\widehat F-F\|_\infty/b+L_fb,
\tag{10}
\]
which tends to zero uniformly for that bandwidth.  Plugging the pilot quantiles, densities, and weight into (2) and the finite covariance sum after (6) therefore gives
\(\widehat\Omega_\ell-\Omega_\ell=o_{\Pr}(1)\) uniformly.  The pilot Gram converges uniformly by the same quantile bound.  The finite-sample strong-curvature calculation in \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\), with \(r_{n,\ell}\) in place of \(n_\ell\), gives \(\widehat w^{P}_\ell-w_\ell=O_{\Pr}(r_{n,\ell}^{-1/2})\) uniformly.

The simplex and the bounded set of covariance matrices are compact.  Hence the extraction in \(\mathrm{lem:local\mbox{-}subsequence\mbox{-}extraction}\) can be refined so that
\[
 w_\ell\to w^0\in\Delta_J,
 \qquad \Omega_\ell\to\Omega.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (6)--(9) then give \(\widehat g^M_\ell\Rightarrow g\sim N_L(0,\Omega)\).  Finally, the main empirical Hessian converges to \(H\), the feasible sets converge to \(D_h\), and \(H|_L\succeq\lambda I_L\).  The variational-inequality subtraction
\[
 \lambda\|v-v'\|_2^2
 \leq \|v-v'\|_2\{2\|g-g'\|_2+|H-H'\|_{\mathrm{op}}(\|v\|_2+\|v'\|_2)\}
\tag{12}
\]
on a common face, followed by the finite active-set enumeration at face changes, proves convergence of the minimizer to \(V_h\).  This establishes all assertions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For pilot sizes \(r_{n,\ell}=\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\), \(r_{m,\ell}=\lceil m_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) and exclusion budget \(\beta_\ell=(n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)^{-2}\), there is a total Borel pilot map that, with probability at least \(1-C\beta_\ell\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), returns a finite union of compact quotient regions containing every true support clustering, covariance rank, simplex face, within-cell offset, unresolved cross-cell translation, and unresolved face offset.  A pilot-unseen post atom has simultaneous mass upper bound \(O(\log(1/\beta_\ell)/r_{m,\ell})=o(m_\ell^{-1/2})\).  If a within-cell atom has mass \(d_{jtr}/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) with bounded \(d_{jtr}\), its pilot root-\(m_\ell\) mass coordinate converges in probability to \(d_{jtr}\), uniformly on compact sets of offsets.  Cross-cell root-\(m_\ell\) translations and root-\(n_\ell\) simplex-face offsets are not plugged in and remain in the certified nuisance supremum.  Conditional on the pilot, the main-sample normalized leading losses admit a uniform bounded-Lipschitz transfer to the compatible Gaussian face--knot experiments, with a computable error envelope tending to zero.  On the certified tail box, exhaustive active-face, endpoint-order, covariance-rank, rational-grid, and bisection enumeration terminates within a deterministic bound
\[
 2^J(2K)!\left\lceil
 C_{\mathrm{cal}}\frac{(1+\sqrt{m_\ell}+G+R)^2}{\zeta_\ell^2}
 \right\rceil^{2(J-1+K)+J+2}
 \left\lceil\log_2\frac{C_{\mathrm{cal}}(1+G+R+\sqrt{m_\ell})}{\zeta_\ell}\right\rceil,
\]
where \(K=(J+1)T_1(S-1)\), \(\zeta_\ell=1/\log(e+n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)\), and \(C_{\mathrm{cal}}\) is the explicit class-constant bound in the proof.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(K_p=(J+1)T_1S\) and put
\[
 L_\ell=\log(8K_p/\beta_\ell),
 \qquad u_\ell=8L_\ell/r_{m,\ell}.
\tag{13}
\]
For an observed pilot atom let \(N\) be its count and \(\widehat p=N/r_{m,\ell}\).  Bernstein's inequality, solved for \(p\), gives the simultaneous interval
\[
 |p-\widehat p|
 \leq 2\sqrt{\widehat pL_\ell/r_{m,\ell}}
       +8L_\ell/r_{m,\ell}.
\tag{14}
\]
For an unobserved atom, \(\Pr_p(N=0)=(1-p)^{r_{m,\ell}}\leq e^{-r_{m,\ell}p}\); hence, except on an event of probability at most \(K_p e^{-r_{m,\ell}u_\ell}\leq\beta_\ell/8\), every unobserved mass is at most \(u_\ell\).  A union bound over the at most \(K_p\) true atoms proves the claimed unseen-mass assertion.  Because
\[
 \sqrt{m_\ell}u_\ell
 =O\!\left(m_\ell^{-1/4}\log(1/\beta_\ell)\right)=o(1),
\tag{15}
\]
omitting or merging such an atom changes a scaled cumulative-mass endpoint by \(o(1)\).  The endpoint Lipschitz bound in \(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\) then makes its normalized loss contribution \(o(1)\), uniformly.

If \(p_\ell=d_{jtr}/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) and \(N_\ell\sim\operatorname{Bin}(r_{m,\ell},p_\ell)\), define \(\widehat d_{jtr,\ell}=\sqrt{m_\ell}N_\ell/r_{m,\ell}\).  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat d_{jtr,\ell}=d_{jtr},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat d_{jtr,\ell})
 =\frac{m_\ell p_\ell(1-p_\ell)}{r_{m,\ell}}
 \leq \frac{d_{jtr}\sqrt{m_\ell}}{r_{m,\ell}}=O(m_\ell^{-1/4}).
\tag{16}
\]
Thus \(\widehat d_{jtr,\ell}\to d_{jtr}\) uniformly for bounded offsets.  Scaling the right side of (14) by \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\) gives
\[
 O_{\Pr}\!\left(m_\ell^{-1/8}\sqrt{L_\ell}
             +m_\ell^{-1/4}L_\ell\right)=o_{\Pr}(1).
\tag{17}
\]
This proves that all within-cell differences made from local intervening masses are learned.  By contrast, a cumulative mass of constant order estimated from an independent cell has pilot error \(O_{\Pr}(r_{m,\ell}^{-1/2})\), which becomes \(O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{1/8})\) after root-\(m_\ell\) scaling.  Likewise the pilot weight error is \(O_{\Pr}(r_{n,\ell}^{-1/2})\), which becomes \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{1/8})\) after root-\(n_\ell\) scaling.  Therefore neither a cross-cell translation nor a face offset is consistently observed.  The construction retains both rather than substituting their pilot centers.

For the pre cells use simultaneous DKW bands with error allocation \(\beta_\ell/8\), the finite-difference density bands from (10), the simplex loss inequality, and interval evaluation of the Gram and influence covariance.  For post cells use (14), allow up to \(S\) atoms, give every unseen atom arbitrary location in the common compact outcome interval and mass in \([0,u_\ell]\), and order observed support points lexicographically by cell, numerical value, and original observation index.  Enumerate all endpoint clusterings, covariance ranks, and simplex faces compatible with these closed intervals.  Quotient one translation in every candidate macro cluster.  Intersect with the simplex, positive-semidefinite, range, density, and \(\lambda\)-curvature constraints.  These operations are finite unions, intersections, projections, and polynomial inequalities in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, so the resulting set, denoted \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\), is compact.  Empirical CDFs, order statistics, finite differences, and the stipulated tie breaks are Borel; projection of each compact semialgebraic cell is compact, and the finite lexicographic enumeration therefore makes \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\) a Borel random closed set.  Equations (13)--(14), DKW, and a union bound give
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P\{(\eta_{P,\ell},\theta_{P,\ell})
                   \in\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\}
 \geq1-C_0\beta_\ell.
\tag{18}
\]

We next establish the conditional raw-to-Gaussian transfer.  The retained main post counts are a fixed-dimensional sum of centered indicator vectors bounded by one.  The characteristic-function calculation (8), now with main size \(N_{m,\ell}=m_\ell-r_{m,\ell}\), gives a Gaussian vector with the exact multinomial covariance, uniformly even when that covariance is singular.  The pre block is handled by \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}linearization}\).  The two blocks are independent by \(\mathrm{ass:cell\mbox{-}independence}\).  With
\[
 d_*=J-1+(J+1)T_1(S-1),
 \qquad \chi=\{8(d_*+4)\}^{-1},
\]
the smoothing calculation used for (9), (4), and the unseen-mass error (15) give the computable envelope
\[
 \gamma_\ell=C_{\mathrm{cal}}\{\log(e+n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)\}^4
 \left(N_{n,\ell}^{-\chi}+N_{m,\ell}^{-\chi}
       +\frac{\sqrt{m_\ell}L_\ell}{r_{m,\ell}}\right)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{19}
\]
where one valid completely explicit choice is
\[
 C_{\mathrm{cal}}=2^{20}(1+J+T_0+T_1+S)^8
 (1+D+f_{\min}^{-1}+f_{\max}+L_f+\lambda^{-1})^8.
\tag{20}
\]
This deliberately loose constant dominates every Taylor, union, and norm-equivalence constant above.

On \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\), comparison with zero gives \(\|V_h\|_2\leq2G/\lambda\).  Subtracting variational inequalities gives (12), so the cone projection is uniformly Lipschitz in the score and Hessian on each enumerated face.  Since \(v\in L\), the outcome-range condition implies \(\|M_t|_L\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq JD^2\).  Thus the quadratic loss has a computable Lipschitz constant on the box.  The endpoint loss has constant at most \((\sum_q|b_q|)^2\leq16D^2\) by \(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\), and a maximum over the fixed \(T_1\) periods preserves Lipschitz continuity.  Consequently (19), a Lipschitz ramp of width \(\delta>0\), and the tail allocation imply, uniformly over all parameters in \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\),
\[
 \Pr\{L^{M,\mathrm{raw}}_\ell\leq c+\delta\mid\text{pilot}\}
 \geq \Pr\{\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\leq c\}
 -C\gamma_\ell L_{G,R}/\delta-\Pr(\mathcal B_{G,R}^c)
 -C\sqrt{m_\ell}u_\ell.
\tag{21}
\]
This is the asserted uniform conditional transfer; no covariance inverse appears.

Choose \(G,R\) by certified Gaussian tail intervals so that the tail in (21) is at most \(\zeta_\ell/8\), and take
\[
 \delta_\ell=4\{(L_{G,R}\gamma_\ell)^{1/2}
                   +\zeta_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}u_\ell\}.
\tag{22}
\]
The covariance bound from (7) shows that the least such integer \(G,R\) are \(O(\sqrt{\log(1/\zeta_\ell)})\); hence \(L_{G,R}\) grows polynomially in \(\log(1/\zeta_\ell)\), and (19) implies \(\delta_\ell\to0\).

It remains to certify finiteness and measurability of the computation.  There are at most \(2^J\) active faces and \((2K)!\) endpoint orders.  After quotienting translations, the joint nuisance--noise dimension is at most \(2(J-1+K)+J\).  Every coordinate lies in an interval of length at most \(C_{\mathrm{cal}}(1+\sqrt{m_\ell}+G+R)\).  A rational mesh smaller than \(\zeta_\ell/[C_{\mathrm{cal}}(1+\sqrt{m_\ell}+G+R)]\), followed by bisection of the loss range, therefore uses no more cells than the displayed bound in the statement.  On each cell, rational interval arithmetic encloses the affine active-set solution, absolute-value endpoint energy, Gaussian linear image, and Gaussian rectangle probability.  The argument of \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}common\mbox{-}cutoff}\) proves that refinement certifies both coverage and the cutoff, including singular-rank and structural-zero cells.  Selecting the first certified rational bracket in the fixed enumeration is Borel.  Taking \(W_\ell\) equal to one plus the displayed deterministic bound makes budget exhaustion impossible whenever the primitive region is certified, and \(W_\ell\to\infty\).  This proves the lemma.

added_lemmas.statement: The array in \(\mathrm{def:j2s3\mbox{-}pilot\mbox{-}instance}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\).  If \(d_{0t2}\) is fixed and \(N_{d,\ell}\) is the pilot count of the treated middle atom, then \(\widehat d_{0t2,\ell}=\sqrt{m_\ell}N_{d,\ell}/r_{m,\ell}\to d_{0t2}\) in probability, whereas every bounded \(h_f\) and \(h_c\) remains in the certified face and cross-cell nuisance region. added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The pre quantiles are \(Q_1(u)=u\) and \(Q_2(u)=u+(2/5)u(1-u)\).  Their derivatives lie in \([3/5,7/5]\).  The inverse densities therefore lie in \([5/7,5/3]\subset[1/2,2]\), and
\[
 |f'(Q(u))|=|Q''(u)|/|Q'(u)|^3
 \leq (4/5)/(3/5)^3=100/27<4.
\tag{32}
\]
The same inequalities hold for every convex combination defining the treated pre law.  For \(v=(a,-a)\in L\),
\[
 v^\top H_\ell v
 =a^2\int_0^1\{Q_1(u)-Q_2(u)\}^2du
 =\frac{4a^2}{25}\int_0^1u^2(1-u)^2du
 =\frac{2a^2}{375}
 =\frac1{375}\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{33}
\]
Thus the smoothness and strong-Gram assumptions hold for \(0<\lambda\leq1/375\).  All post masses are nonnegative under the displayed bounds, every observed post law has at most three atoms in \([0,2]\), and cell samples are independent.  The pre and post no-intervention equalities use the same \(w_\ell\) by construction.  Hence every defining assumption of \(\mathcal M\) holds.

The middle-atom count is binomial with parameters \(r_{m,\ell}\) and \(d_{0t2}/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), so (16) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat d_{0t2,\ell}=d_{0t2},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat d_{0t2,\ell})
 =\frac{d_{0t2}\sqrt{m_\ell}}{r_{m,\ell}}
   \left(1-\frac{d_{0t2}}{\sqrt{m_\ell}}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{34}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality proves \(\widehat d_{0t2,\ell}\to d_{0t2}\).  In contrast, the independent pilot estimates forming \(h_c\) have root-\(m_\ell\) noise of order \(m_\ell^{1/8}\), and the pilot weight estimate forming \(h_f\) has root-\(n_\ell\) noise of order \(n_\ell^{1/8}\).  Thus the procedure correctly conditions on (34) but retains \(h_c\) and \(h_f\) in its supremum.  The stratum is supported by the legal array just verified.  Applying \(\mathrm{thm:pilot\mbox{-}split\mbox{-}certified\mbox{-}attainment}\), with the terminating calculation from \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}common\mbox{-}cutoff}\), proves vanishing fallback, conditional cutoff convergence, and the certified interval assertion.

proposed.name: Total pilot-split certified QTE radius
proposed.construction:
For each cell, assign the first \(r_{n,\ell}=\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) pre observations and the first \(r_{m,\ell}=\lceil m_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) post observations to a pilot, with the original observation order breaking all ties; use the remaining \(N_{n,\ell}=n_\ell-r_{n,\ell}\) and \(N_{m,\ell}=m_\ell-r_{m,\ell}\) observations for a main-sample QTE center \(\widetilde\tau_{t,\ell}\).  Put \(\beta_\ell=(n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)^{-2}\) and \(\zeta_\ell=1/\log(e+n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)\).  Construct the simultaneous pilot random closed set \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\) by the binomial, DKW, density-difference, Gram, covariance, support-cluster, covariance-rank, and simplex-face intervals in \(\mathrm{lem:pilot\mbox{-}geometry\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}transfer}\).  Every unresolved root-\(m_\ell\) cross-cell translation and root-\(n_\ell\) face offset is retained; only the pilot-consistent within-cell offset differences are conditioned upon.  Choose certified Gaussian tail bounds \(G,R\), compute the transfer cushion \(\delta_\ell\) from equation~(22) of that lemma, and use exhaustive rational interval arithmetic over \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\cap\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\) to return the upper endpoint \(\overline c_\ell\) of a cutoff bracket of width at most \(\zeta_\ell\).  Let \(a^M_\ell=N_{n,\ell}^{-1}+N_{m,\ell}^{-1/2}\), let \(T^\circ_\ell=\max_{t>T_0}\|\widetilde\tau_{t,\ell}-\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}\), and on successful certification set
\[
 R_\ell=\min\{2D,\sqrt{a^M_\ell(\overline c_\ell+\delta_\ell)}+T^\circ_\ell\}.
\]
Take \(W_\ell\) to be one plus the deterministic grid-complexity bound in \(\mathrm{lem:pilot\mbox{-}geometry\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}transfer}\).  If a main block is empty, a primitive region fails its deterministic checks, or certification has not succeeded by \(W_\ell\) operations, set \(R_\ell=R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell\).  All enumerations use the fixed lexicographic ordering and the first certified rational bracket, so this defines one total Borel function of the data.

prose_updates.tldr: Exact discrete distributional synthetic control identifies the treated unit's no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period with one stable simplex weight. Its QTE estimator has two first-order error sources on different scales: an exact finite-array signed endpoint energy from empirical post-period atoms and a cone-projected quadratic from simplex weight estimation. The exact squared-error decomposition also retains the pre-weight--post-quantile cross term and three donor-quantile remainder terms; pulse geometry makes them vanish under every headline normalization. Uniform identification is imposed on the finite-array Grams \(H_\ell\), while \(H\), the limiting weight \(w^0\), and the triangular pre-score covariance \(\Omega\) enter only after local-subsequence extraction. The project proves rate-optimal uniformly honest simultaneous \(L^2\) QTE balls and the least common deterministic conditional cutoff. A pilot split of sizes \(\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) and \(\lceil m_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\), simultaneous primitive regions, exhaustive support/rank/face enumeration, certified rational Gaussian calculation, explicit error budgets, and a deterministic work bound now give one total measurable radius that attains this conditional cutoff on every supported fixed local stratum, with a vanishing DKW fallback. Root-post-sample within-cell masses are learned, whereas cross-cell translations and simplex-face offsets remain in the nuisance supremum. Oracle calibration occurs only on separated interior strata with continuous nondegenerate critical law. The Bernoulli 95 percent honesty bracket \((1.913,1.914]\), versus collision-oracle value \(1.38590382435\), proves that the nonregular honesty penalty cannot be adapted away.

project_justification.gap: Chen's published DSC identifies counterfactuals by pre-intervention quantile-residual matching, Gunsilius supplies the quantile-span model and discrete goodness-of-fit asymptotics, and Alvarez--Orestes gives direct DSC inference under smooth continuous-cell and donor-dilution conditions. None supplies a measurable uniformly honest radius that combines an exact stable post-treatment no-intervention span, atomic endpoint conditioning, estimated simplex faces, changing covariance rank, primitive nuisance exclusion, uniform raw-to-Gaussian transfer, and certified common-cutoff attainment; no formula-level claim about Gunsilius Proposition~5 is used because its version-of-record equation was inaccessible.
project_justification.niche: Fixed donors, independent pre and post cell samples, one exact span weight across all pre-treatment and post-treatment no-intervention laws, and finite-support post laws generate a two-scale face--knot experiment. A root-three-quarter pilot learns limiting design, covariance, support, and within-cell local mass gaps, while root-scale cross-cell translations and face offsets remain nuisance. The main sample supplies the QTE center, and a certified finite-dimensional nuisance supremum preserves honesty through collisions, covariance-rank changes, and simplex boundaries.
project_justification.fill: The paper fills the gap with the exact six-term finite-array loss decomposition, pulse-sharp cross-term control, triangular pre-score linearization with explicit covariance, three phase laws, component degeneracy criteria, rate-optimal DKW fallback, Bernoulli honesty penalty, conditional minimax common-cutoff calculation, and one total Borel pilot-split certified radius. Simultaneous primitive regions with exclusion budget \(\beta_\ell=(n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)^{-2}\), exhaustive compatible support/rank/face enumeration, Gaussian transfer and tail cushions, rational interval arithmetic, and a deterministic work bound yield uniform asymptotic coverage, conditional cutoff convergence, and vanishing fallback on supported fixed local strata.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The first \(\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) pre observations and \(\lceil m_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) post observations in every cell form a deterministic pilot; the remaining observations form the independent main-sample center. Simultaneous CDF, variance-adaptive multinomial-mass, density-difference, Gram, weight, and covariance regions are combined with deterministic support, covariance-rank, and simplex-face enumeration. Within-cell root-post-sample mass gaps are consistently learned, including pilot-unseen-mass control, while cross-cell knot translations and root-pre-sample face offsets stay in the certified nuisance supremum. The matrix \(H\), limiting weight \(w^0\), and covariance \(\Omega\) appear only after local-subsequence extraction.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen's Journal of Applied Econometrics article is a direct DSC comparator: it identifies counterfactuals by matching treated pre-intervention quantile residuals to a convex combination of control residuals. Gunsilius establishes the Wasserstein-quantile DSC model and a discrete goodness-of-fit result, while Alvarez and Orestes treat smooth continuous empirical quantiles with ridge regularization and donor dilution. Zhang, Zhang, and Zhang study prediction and weight rates under quantile-grid and interior-weight conditions; Sommerfeld and Munk provide finite-space Wasserstein directional limits; and Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, Melly, and Wuthrich project distribution bands into discrete quantile bands. Andrews supplies tangent-cone extremum asymptotics, Canen and Song address simplex-weight inference, Andrews and Mikusheva develop Gaussian nuisance conditioning, and Cox and Shi enumerate active constraints. Robins and van der Vaart and Hoffmann and Nickl establish general honesty-versus-adaptation obstructions. These works supply separate model, empirical-process, conditional-Gaussian, active-set, and honesty ingredients, but none states the present measurable pilot-split theorem: uniform raw-sample-to-Gaussian transfer through atomic support and covariance-rank changes, certified nuisance exclusion over cross-cell translations and simplex faces, a total common-cutoff radius, and vanishing fallback. Zhai et al. remain the same-question consumer for raw discrete mosquito-abundance QTE curves; their separate binary CDF and \(W_1\) elimination analysis is outside scope.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The local criterion minimizes only the common deterministic conditional squared-radius cutoff over \(\mathscr C_\eta\); it does not optimize expected radius, randomized rules, or arbitrary observation-dependent radius rules. The finite Gaussian object is a conditional leading-loss experiment, not an unrestricted deficiency equivalence for the raw samples. The pilot-split theorem supplies the uniform transfer needed for this radius and keeps an explicit vanishing cushion for linearization, nuisance exclusion, Gaussian tails, and numerical enclosure. The sharper cross term is nondegenerate only at its own finer scale and does not alter the cutoff. Cross-cell translations and face offsets remain nuisance near collisions and boundaries, and oracle calibration is asserted only on fixed separated interior strata with continuous nondegenerate critical law. Applying the result to Zhai et al. would additionally require a bridge for discrete pre-period outcomes, beta-weighted quantile fitting, period aggregation, spatial dependence, and interpolation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact endpoint identity, exact six-term finite-array squared-error decomposition, pulse-sharp cross-vector limit, diagonal local compactification, triangular pre-score linearization with limiting weight \(w^0\) and covariance \(\Omega\), normalized compound loss, coupled three-phase limits, component degeneracy criteria, DKW upper rate, matching richness-conditional lower rate, Bernoulli honesty penalty, deterministic common cutoff, and pilot-split certified attainment theorem are proved. The stable-span model identifies \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}\) with the same \(w_\ell\) in every pre-treatment and post-treatment no-intervention period; it never equates the counterfactual law with \(Q^I_{0t,\ell}\). The total measurable radius is uniformly asymptotically honest and rate-optimal, has vanishing fallback on supported fixed local strata, learns within-cell local offsets, and converges conditionally to the common deterministic cutoff while retaining cross-cell translations and face offsets as nuisance. Oracle calibration is claimed only under fixed unscaled knot separation, weights bounded away from every face, and a continuous nondegenerate critical law. The Bernoulli calculation proves the unavoidable honesty penalty near collisions; no adaptation to the smaller collision-oracle cutoff is claimed. The result does not optimize randomized or general observation-dependent radii and does not cover Zhai et al.'s separate binary elimination estimand.
